   - For \( 7 \le x < 8 \), \( \lfloor x \rfloor = 7 \). The greatest prime factor of 7 is 7. So, \( p(x) = p(7) + (x + 1 - 7) = p(7) + (x - 6) \).
   - For \( 8 \le x < 9 \), \( \lfloor x \rfloor = 8 \). The greatest prime factor of 8 is 2. So, \( p(x) = p(8) + (x + 1 - 8) = p(8) + (x - 7) \).
   - For \( 9 \le x < 10 \), \( \lfloor x \rfloor = 9 \). The greatest prime factor of 9 is 3. So, \( p(x) = p(9) + (x + 1 - 9) = p(9) + (x - 8) \).

2. **Determine the values of \( p(x) \) for each interval:**
   - For \( 2 \le x < 3 \), \( p(x) = p(2) + (x - 1) \). Since \( p(2) = 2 + 1 = 3 \), \( p(x) = 3 + (x - 1) = x + 2 \).

   - For \( 7 \le x < 8 \), \( p(x) = p(7) + (x - 6) \). Since \( p(7) = 7 + 1 = 8 \), \( p(x) = 8 + (x - 6) = x + 2 \).

   - For \( 9 \le x < 10 \), \( p(x) = p(9) + (x - 8) \). Since \( p(9) = 9 + 1 = 10 \), \( p(x) = 10 + (x - 8) = x + 2 \).

3. **Determine the range of \( p(x) \):**
   - The function \( p(x) = x + 2 \) is a linear function that increases by 1 for each increment of \( x \) in the interval \( 2 \le x < 10 \).
